title: Identifying subtypes of chronic kidney disease with machine learning: development, internal validation and prognostic validation using linked electronic health records in 350,067 individuals
summary: Seven unsupervised clustering methods on linked EHR features identified five CKD profiles; XGBoost predicted subtype labels. Across incident and prevalent CKD cohorts (350,067 and 195,422), five profiles (early-onset, late-onset, cancer, metabolic, cardiometabolic) differed in 5-year mortality, admissions and incident chronic disease. Cardiometabolic incident subtype had highest 5-year mortality/admission risks; this is observational prognostic stratification, not causal etiology. Population-based UK EHR development; internal clustering/method consistency and prognostic validation across linked outcomes. No independent external geography validation, a limitation stated by authors. This record is limited to the study result and does not establish independent replication or real-world benefit.
